title: KV cache inspector playpad
content:
Quick context / why this exists:

We have pretty opaque per-session state in the runtime (KV cache, chunked attention caches, prefix caches). Engineers repeatedly ask: what was actually stored in the cache for a session? why did a re-run of the same prompt produce a different token stream? why did cache growth cause a latency spike?

Hypothesis: a lightweight KV Cache Inspector (dev-only UI + lightweight API) will make debugging session-level anomalies MUCH faster, reduce triage time, and help product teams craft better cache-friendly prompts. It also helps when designing cache eviction and serialization for Private deployments.

Goals:
- Surface what keys/entries exist in a session's KV cache at a glance (counts, sizes, age).
- Allow replay/inspect of specific cache keys (first N bytes / tokens) without pulling full blobs into console logs.
- Correlate cache mutations (writes/evictions) with incoming request IDs and timestamps.
- Provide heuristics to highlight 'hot' entries and surprising growth patterns.
- Minimal perf impact: read-only inspector should be cheap and opt-in.

Primary users / personas:
- Runtime engineers: triaging weird outputs / seq2seq divergence.
- Solutions/SEs debugging customer private installs.
- Product managers / PMMs who want to understand common failure modes for session-heavy flows.
- Reliability engineers investigating latency regressions caused by cache pressure.

Core user stories (MVP):
1) As a runtime engineer, I want to open a session by id and see a summarized view: total KV entries, total bytes, top-5 entries by size, last-write time, so I can quickly assess whether cache size is plausible.
2) As a solutions engineer, I want to view the last 10 mutations to a session's KV cache with request ids and timestamps, so I can map a customer request to the cache change.
3) As an SRE, I want to see a timeline graph of per-session cache size over the last 5 minutes for a particular host, so I can correlate with CPU/GPU utilization.
4) As a runtime dev, I want to peek at the first 256 tokens or hex-dump of a given key (scrubbed by default) to validate whether keys are storing expected prefixes.
5) As a PM, I want an automated 'suspicious growth' alert rule (e.g., >3x size increase in 60s) that lists candidate sessions to investigate.

MVP surface / featureset:
- API: GET /inspector/sessions/{session_id}/summary -> JSON summary (counts, bytes, last_mutation)
- API: GET /inspector/sessions/{session_id}/keys -> paginated list of keys with meta (size, type tag, last_write)
- API: GET /inspector/sessions/{session_id}/keys/{key_id}?peek=256 -> returns sanitized preview
- Lightweight UI embedded in Console: session inspector drawer with three panes (summary, timeline, key list / peek)
- Server-side toggle: inspector-read-mode = on|off per deployment/customer (default off in Private)
- RBAC: inspector only available to allowed roles (devs, SE) and requires audit logging

Data & telemetry considerations:
- Peeks must be scrubbed by default (PII filter) and only show token-level previews, not entire raw blobs.
- All inspector accesses must be audited and show in customer audit logs for Private deployments.
- Read paths must sample or rate-limit on high-traffic hosts to avoid perf regressions.
- Storage: central index of session -> key metadata should be kept separate from full blobs; avoid duplicating large objects.

Design sketch (text):
- Top bar: session id, model, created_at, current cache size
- Left pane: summary cards (entries, bytes, hot keys, median ttl) and quick actions (force-evict, mark-for-review)
- Middle pane: timeline (line chart) with overlay of request RPS; hover shows mutation events
- Right pane: key list table with type tags (kv, attention-kv, prefix), size, last write, peek button
- Peek modal: shows sanitized token preview + origin request id + timestamp + button to copy obfuscated sample

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Inspecting a session summary returns in < 150ms for cold lookups and <25ms for hot lookups (bench target).
- Peeking a key returns only preview up to 256 tokens and strips tokens flagged by PII heuristics.
- No additional full-blob copies are created during normal inspection; all reads are stream/peeked.
- Audit log entries are created for each peek and visible in console under session activity.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we tag key types reliably across all model formats (LLM families, kv naming conventions)? Need standard key metadata at write time.
- Privacy: even sanitized previews could leak sensitive info. For hosted offering, do we allow peeks at all? Maybe limited to internal devs only; customers can opt-in.
- Perf: reading many keys could stress mem/disk. Consider sampling, async index, or read-only background snapshots.
- Storage cost: maintaining per-session metadata index adds cost. Keep only last N sessions per host by default.
- Backwards compatibility: older sessions may not have metadata; inspector should degrade gracefully.

Implementation notes / rough plan:
- Phase 0: infra spike - build a tiny service that exposes a read-only view into an existing session store (work on a non-prod clone). Add lightweight metadata index (key counts, sizes, last_write).
- Phase 1: API + CLI only. Endpoint to fetch summary + list + peek. Basic RBAC, audit logging.
- Phase 2: Console UI + timeline chart, integrate with tracing (request ids), add suspicious-growth rule writer.
- Phase 3: Hardening for Private (opt-in, audit hooks, PII policy), sampling controls for hosted.

Short-term next steps (this week):
- Talk to runtime team (Lena) to confirm what metadata is already emitted (key tagging, write timestamps).
- Create an infra spike ticket: jira/INFR-7891 (linked above) and attach a minimal data model sketch.
- Prototype API in a sidecar (sana/kv-inspector-proto) using an in-memory index.
- Add a short Slack poll in #runtime-observability: who needs key-peek today?

Notes to self / brain dump:
- Could be extremely useful for model onboarding: model-specific cache footprints will be visible per-session.
- Might integrate with Optimize suggestions: when inspector shows frequent large prefix keys, recommend prefix trimming or quantization.
- Consider an "explain cache hit" button: given a token emission, show which key(s) contributed to KV hits (harder — requires instrumentation at generation time).

Mini checklist:
- [ ] Confirm available metadata from write path with serving-runtime
- [ ] Spike service and basic index
- [ ] Implement APIs and CLI for devs
- [ ] Add PII scrubber library integration
- [ ] Wire basic Console drawer + timeline
- [ ] Run perf tests and set sampling defaults

Random ideas for future iterations:
- Allow recording of a 'cache snapshot' bundle that can be attached to a support ticket (with customer consent) for offline replay.
- A diff view that shows what changed between two session snapshots.
- Heatmap merging of hot keys across customers to discover common prefixes to optimize kernel selection.

End of scratchpad.
